ingredients.item: Yangnyeom ganjang , the scallion-soy dip, in a bowl the table shares

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Hot grate or pan, single layer, two minutes undisturbed. The shells take light char at the tips; the smell is garlic and sesame over toasting shell.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the shells blush and the bottom edges char thinly; lift one — the meat below should be opaque more than halfway up.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip once, 60–90 seconds, off the fire the moment the last translucence at the center of a test shrimp is gone.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: pull one and cut: opaque white through, still plump and springy. Shrimp's overcook line is 30 seconds past this point — the grill boss eats the test piece standing up, as is right.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Platter, and the dip is half the dish: yangnyeom ganjang (#SA04), scallions heavy, each shrimp dunked at the table.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test: snap, sweetness, soy-garlic roundness, the dip's scallion bite — shrimp first, seasoning behind, always. This lane exists to let the shrimp talk.

storageNotes: Raw marinated shrimp hold 30 minutes. Cooked, 2 days — cold peeled shrimp over rice or into a light noodle bowl; shells to stock.
Variations: a pinch of gochugaru in the marinade to walk toward the spicy fork (#SF01); butter in the final minute for the fusion table; the same marinade on the squid record's clean cousin lanes.
